season_storylines: Patrick Mahomes is fully cleared for camp off his Week 15 2025 torn ACL and is targeting the Sept 14 opener vs Denver, so his 6-pt-passing-TD premium is intact but his rushing ceiling off a reconstructed knee is the real risk to price in.

The 2026 coaching carousel was massive: John Harbaugh to the Giants, Kevin Stefanski to the Falcons, Todd Monken to the Browns, Mike McCarthy to the Steelers, Klint Kubiak to the Raiders, Robert Saleh (with Brian Daboll as OC) to the Titans, and Mike LaFleur to the Cardinals, each dragging run/pass identity and pace with them.

Kyler Murray was dealt to Minnesota and has been named the Week 1 starter over J.J. McCarthy (73 vs 38 first-team snaps), restoring a rushing-QB ceiling that fits 6-pt TD, -2 INT scoring far better than McCarthy's profile.

Kenneth Walker III is now the Chiefs' lead back under new OC Eric Bieniemy with Emari Demercado the preferred backup, giving Walker goal-line equity in a top-10 scoring offense, the exact profile non-PPR leagues pay for.

Josh Jacobs carries a double red flag: a groin injury costing him a week of camp and an open domestic-violence investigation that could bring a 6-game Personal Conduct suspension, so his TD-heavy floor could vanish in one league memo (verify suspension timing).

Malik Nabers had a second offseason surgery to clean up scar tissue from his 2025 ACL tear and his Week 1 vs Dallas is not assured, which props up Isaiah Likely and Cam Skattebo TD shares in John Harbaugh's run-leaning Giants offense.

San Francisco's pass-catcher room is in chaos: Ricky Pearsall is out for the season (PCL), rookie De'Zhaun Stribling and Christian Kirk are banged up, Deebo Samuel was re-signed, and George Kittle (Achilles) sits on PUP with a stated Week 1 goal but a 4-plus-week minimum if he stays there.

Tua Tagovailoa signed with Atlanta and is positioned to start with Michael Penix Jr. still not cleared for team drills after knee surgery, keeping Bijan Robinson's volume in Stefanski's zone-run scheme the safest asset in that building.

A.J. Brown was acquired by New England, giving Drake Maye a true alpha deep threat and pushing buzzy Kayshon Boutte into a best-ball-only role; in non-PPR, Brown's air-yards profile travels perfectly.

Betting markets frame the year: Ravens and Rams sit at a league-high 11.5 wins while Miami and Arizona sit at 3.5, so DST streamers and kicker picks should lean hard into that gap (Brandon Aubrey and his record six 60-plus-yard FGs is the distance-scoring cheat code).

teams.outlook: New HC Mike LaFleur inherits a 3.5-win-total teardown after the Kyler Murray trade, so treat Cardinals skill players as TD-starved; rookie RB Jeremiyah Love currently sits behind Tyler Allgeier on the depth chart (verify) and Michael Wilson is the only proven target earner.

Kevin Stefanski and OC Tommy Rees bring a zone-run identity and Tua Tagovailoa likely starts with Penix not cleared, making Bijan Robinson a top-3 non-PPR pick on volume plus goal-line work while Zachariah Branch adds PR/KR return-yardage juice.

New HC Jesse Minter kept the offense aggressive by importing OC Declan Doyle, whose creativity has Lamar Jackson energized; camp says Zay Flowers is the focal point, and his yards-per-route profile with TD regression coming his way is a non-PPR buy.

Joe Brady's promotion to HC preserves continuity for Josh Allen and James Cook, and D.J. Moore is impressing as the steady X Buffalo has lacked since Diggs, a yardage-and-TD role that fits this scoring.

Bryce Young keeps improving and Tetairoa McMillan (122 rookie targets) is the clear alpha, while Chuba Hubbard's injury has handed camp momentum and likely the early-down/goal-line role to a healthy Jonathon Brooks.

Ben Johnson retains play-calling with Press Taylor as OC so no schematic regression is expected, but Luther Burden III (groin, likely out all preseason) and the D.J. Moore departure concentrate targets on Rome Odunze and TE Colston Loveland (verify Odunze role).

Cincinnati is installing more under-center play-action and it looks rough in camp, but Burrow-to-Chase remains the league's premier TD pipeline and Evan McPherson keeps distance-kicking value; watch rookie Colbie Young pushing Iosivas for WR3.

New HC Todd Monken is rotating Deshaun Watson and Shedeur Sanders with neither seizing the job (Dillon Gabriel lurking), so the only Browns asset to trust is Quinshon Judkins behind four new offensive line starters.

A 9.5-win offense with Brandon Aubrey, the No. 1 kicker in distance-scoring formats after six 60-plus-yard FGs, and explosive Jaydon Blue trending toward RB2 work plus kickoff returns, a sneaky non-PPR stack of TD and return yardage.

Bo Nix is healthy and thriving under new OC Davis Webb's quick-game, the trade for Jaylen Waddle (leg strain, back next week) adds a vertical separator, and Marvin Mims now pairs real offensive snaps with elite PR/KR yardage.

New OC Drew Petzing inherits a loaded unit that just made Jahmyr Gibbs the highest-paid RB ever, with Isiah Pacheco (MCL sprain, expected Week 1) as the thunder; Jake Bates remains a top distance-scoring kicker in a high-total offense.

Josh Jacobs (groin, plus open legal case with 6-game suspension risk) clouds the backfield, Tucker Kraft is off PUP with a shot at Week 1, and Matthew Golden is catching everything in his Year 2 breakout window.
C.J. Stroud gets Tank Dell back in pads for the first time since 2024 and Jaylin Noel steps into the primary slot with PR/KR duties, while Ka'imi Fairbairn remains a top-2 kicker in distance formats.

Daniel Jones looks excellent eight months post-Achilles and is taking every first-team rep in Shane Steichen's offense, and with Michael Pittman traded away Josh Downs' 27.6% target rate makes him the target hog, though slot volume plays down in non-PPR.

Parker Washington has ascended to the top of the target pecking order (team-high 58 catches last year plus PR yardage), Travis Hunter is leaning defense (51 defensive vs 35 offensive reps), and rookie-contract RB Bhayshul Tuten has a real path to RB1 touches plus kick returns.

Mahomes is cleared and targeting Week 1, new OC Eric Bieniemy hands Kenneth Walker III the lead job with goal-line equity, and Rashee Rice is cleared physically but carries unresolved legal risk after 30 days of jail time with no NFL ruling yet.

Mike McDaniel arrives as OC to inject speed-in-space efficiency for Justin Herbert, Ladd McConkey and ascending Omarion Hampton, and the market is buying it (10.5 win total with over steam), though the left guard spot is a five-man mess.
A league-high 11.5 win total with Matthew Stafford praising camp quality and Puka Nacua's groin issue considered minor means the Rams' TD ecosystem is stable and priced accordingly.

New HC Klint Kubiak brings his wide-zone run scheme to Ashton Jeanty, which is exactly the volume-plus-TD profile this scoring rewards, with Kirk Cousins safely ahead of rookie Fernando Mendoza and Brock Bowers targeted heavily.

Post-Tua, a 3.5-win rebuild under new HC Jeff Hafley with an unsettled QB and WR pecking order means only De'Von Achane's fit in OC Bobby Slowik's zone scheme and Malik Washington's PR/KR yardage are investable.

Kyler Murray was named the Week 1 starter over J.J. McCarthy after dominating first-team snaps, restoring rushing-QB ceiling to a receiving corps led by Justin Jefferson (verify JJ health) in a 6-pt passing TD league.

The blockbuster A.J. Brown acquisition gives Drake Maye a contested-catch alpha whose air-yardage profile is gold in non-PPR, pushing camp darling Kayshon Boutte into a rotational role; Marcus Jones and Kyle Williams hold the return jobs.

Newly signed Travis Etienne is taking the early-down work with Alvin Kamara shifted to passing downs (a demotion in non-PPR terms), and top-10 rookie Jordyn Tyson plus returner Barion Brown are the upside plays after Ja'Lynn Polk's retirement.

John Harbaugh and OC Matt Nagy signal a run-first identity built on Cam Skattebo, with Jaxson Dart's rushing TDs carrying 6-pt-TD ceiling, Isaiah Likely imported as a top-two target, and Malik Nabers' Week 1 uncertain after a second ACL cleanup surgery.

New OC Frank Reich's run-game emphasis funnels everything through Breece Hall on a 5.5-win team, with Isaiah Davis pushing Braelon Allen for the handcuff role and TE Kenyon Sadiq's hernia setback opening snaps for Jelani Woods.

New OC Sean Mannion is shifting the Eagles under center and Jalen Hurts has shined since pads came on, but DeVonta Smith's recurring hamstring bears watching; the tush-push goal-line monopoly keeps Hurts and Saquon Barkley TD-rich (verify Barkley usage).

Mike McCarthy reunites with Aaron Rodgers (verify Rodgers as Week 1 starter) in a familiarity play, and camp says Rico Dowdle, not the listed depth chart, is poised to lead the backfield timeshare, making him a cheap non-PPR volume bet.

Losing play-caller Klint Kubiak to Vegas (Brian Fleury promoted for continuity) dents the passing efficiency, Zach Charbonnet is on PUP, and with Kenneth Walker gone the backfield is open for Hard Knocks star Jadarian Price while Tory Horton stacks targets plus both return jobs.

Kyle Shanahan's room is battered: Pearsall out for the year, Kittle on PUP with a Week 1 goal, Deebo re-signed and rookie Stribling hurt, so Christian McCaffrey plus Jordan Mason's league-best missed-tackle metrics carry the TD load (verify Mason/Aaron Jones roles).

New OC Zac Robinson brings McVay-tree structure Baker Mayfield trusts, Bucky Irving pairs a lead role with kickoff returns for extra yardage points, Emeka Egbuka's toe is minor, and the Vita Vea contract standoff is the locker-room wildcard.

Robert Saleh hired Brian Daboll to run the offense and Cam Ward is playing mistake-free ball after a 10-TD/1-INT close to 2025, with rookie Carnell Tate, Wan'Dale Robinson, camp star Elic Ayomanor (shoulder being evaluated) and all-purpose returner Chimere Dike around him.

Stefon Diggs signed on as the WR2 opposite Terry McLaurin, whose under-center play-action usage is being ramped up, and camp reports say Jacory Croskey-Merritt has passed Rachaad White for lead-back duties in Jayden Daniels' TD-rich offense.

breakout_watch.name: Jaxson Dart
breakout_watch.why: Averaged 20-plus fantasy points per game as a rookie with 487 rush yards and 9 rush TDs in 12 starts; 6-pt passing TDs plus rushing floor make him a top-10 QB bet, and Nabers/Skattebo/Likely all upgrade his 2026 supporting cast.

breakout_watch.name: Cam Ward
breakout_watch.why: Threw 10 TDs to 1 INT after his Week 10 bye and nearly doubled his points per attempt, and the high-TD low-INT trajectory under new OC Brian Daboll is exactly what 6-pt TD, -2 INT scoring pays for.

breakout_watch.name: Cam Skattebo
breakout_watch.why: John Harbaugh's Giants are signaling a run-first identity built around him; he forced a missed tackle on 29.2% of carries, and a bell-cow with goal-line work is the single most valuable archetype in non-PPR.

breakout_watch.name: Quinshon Judkins
breakout_watch.why: Earned 93.3% of his rushing yards after contact behind a terrible line, and Cleveland added four new OL starters under run-focused Todd Monken; pure rushing-yardage-and-TD profile, no reception dependency.

breakout_watch.name: Jonathon Brooks
breakout_watch.why: Finally healthy off multiple ACL rehabs with all-positive camp chatter, and Chuba Hubbard's injury clears the early-down and goal-line path in Carolina; being held out of the Hall of Fame game was precautionary.

breakout_watch.name: Bhayshul Tuten
breakout_watch.why: Camp reporting gives him a legitimate chance to emerge as Jacksonville's RB1 while also holding kick-return duties, stacking rushing TDs with return yardage that scores in this league.

breakout_watch.name: Jacory Croskey-Merritt
breakout_watch.why: Washington reportedly prefers him to Rachaad White as the lead runner in a Jayden Daniels offense that manufactures red-zone trips, and he has been developed as a three-down option.

breakout_watch.name: Jaydon Blue
breakout_watch.why: Explosive camp with a realistic path to Dallas RB2 work plus kickoff returns; speed-based big plays and return yardage beat catch-count compilers in this format.

breakout_watch.name: Zay Flowers
breakout_watch.why: Top-three in yards per route run among 300-plus-route players but only 5 TDs in 2025, and camp says he is the focal point of the Ravens passing game; positive TD regression in a Lamar offense is a non-PPR cheat code.

breakout_watch.name: Tetairoa McMillan
breakout_watch.why: 122 rookie targets on an Amari Cooper/Julio-style trajectory with Bryce Young improving across efficiency metrics; alpha X receivers who win downfield and in the end zone are what this scoring rewards.

breakout_watch.name: Matthew Golden
breakout_watch.why: Catching everything in Green Bay camp with a Year 2 leap brewing, and Jayden Reed's ankle plus Jacobs' uncertainty could concentrate TD equity; his toe issue is only day-to-day.

breakout_watch.name: Jordyn Tyson
breakout_watch.why: Top-8 draft capital going as WR35 in the ninth round; recent top-8 rookie WRs average 14-plus points per game, and the Saints' target vacuum after Polk's retirement leaves him a clear runway.

breakout_watch.name: Tory Horton
breakout_watch.why: Seattle camp hype is back after an injury-lost season and he has a realistic chance at both return jobs plus offensive snaps, layering 2.5-3.4 ppg of return yardage on top of deep-ball upside.

breakout_watch.name: Isaiah Likely
breakout_watch.why: Signed with the Giants as the No. 2 target and only Kittle beats his efficiency profile since 2022 (8.1 yards per target); a TD-dependent TE is fine when TDs are the whole game in non-PPR.

fade_watch.name: Rashee Rice
fade_watch.why: Cleared physically but served 30 days in jail this May for a probation violation and the NFL has not ruled yet; an in-season suspension would zero out weeks, and his slot-heavy catch volume is already discounted in non-PPR.

fade_watch.name: Josh Jacobs
fade_watch.why: Groin injury plus an open domestic-violence investigation carrying baseline 6-game suspension exposure, on top of a heavy recent workload; the range of outcomes is too wide for his draft price (verify NFL ruling timing).

fade_watch.name: Chuba Hubbard
fade_watch.why: Injured while Jonathon Brooks wins camp; he already lost lead work to Rico Dowdle once, and losing goal-line touches strips the only thing that made him valuable in this format.

fade_watch.name: Sam Darnold
fade_watch.why: Lost play-caller Klint Kubiak to the Raiders head job, and career evidence says his efficiency is scheme-dependent; with -2 INTs, his turnover tail is the exact risk this scoring punishes (verify Seattle QB depth chart).

fade_watch.name: Rachaad White
fade_watch.why: Washington reportedly prefers Croskey-Merritt as the lead back, and White's value has always been reception-driven, which is worth zero here.

fade_watch.name: Alvin Kamara
fade_watch.why: Shifted to third-down and passing-situation work behind newly signed Travis Etienne; a catch-heavy age-31 role on a rebuilding team is close to worthless at zero PPR.

fade_watch.name: Braelon Allen
fade_watch.why: Isaiah Davis is pushing him for the Jets' No. 2 job behind Breece Hall in Frank Reich's run game, so he may not even own the handcuff role his ADP assumes.

fade_watch.name: Brian Thomas Jr.
fade_watch.why: Parker Washington has seized the top of the Jacksonville target pecking order in camp; Thomas keeps the vertical role, which softens the blow in non-PPR, but his early-round price assumed target dominance he may not get.

fade_watch.name: Oronde Gadsden II
fade_watch.why: Third in Miami's TE pecking order behind Njoku and Kolar because of blocking, in an offense with an unsettled QB room and a 3.5-win total, so the TD math never gets there.

uncertainty_note: Mid-August depth charts are still preseason artifacts: the biggest open questions are whether Mahomes, Nabers, Kittle and Tucker Kraft are actually on the field Week 1, how the league rules on Josh Jacobs and Rashee Rice (no suspensions announced as of Aug 14), who starts at QB for Cleveland's three-man rotation and Miami's post-Tua room, and whether camp-report role wins (Croskey-Merritt over White, Dowdle leading Pittsburgh, Parker Washington as Jacksonville's No. 1, Tuten as RB1) survive preseason games; several relocations reported by single sources are flagged (verify) inside the brief.
